questions.q: What does observability add on top of monitoring?
options: Context that explains why symptoms happen and what to do
questions.explain: Monitoring shows symptoms (numbers, thresholds). Observability interprets them in context so they become actionable.

questions.q: A smartwatch says "You've averaged low sleep this week — wind down earlier." Which concept does this illustrate?
questions.explain: Using patterns over time to give meaningful advice is the course's example of observability. A single threshold alert would be monitoring.

questions.q: Which are the three pillars of observability?
questions.explain: Metrics, logs, and traces. Dynatrace also captures security, business, and deployment events beyond them.

questions.q: A checkout request took 6 s. Which data shows exactly which component the time was spent in?
questions.explain: Traces follow a single request through every component and show where time was spent.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of an ActiveGate?
options: Act as a secure relay between many OneAgents and the Dynatrace platform
questions.explain: OneAgents send to the ActiveGate, which forwards data securely — fewer firewall rules and scalable routing.

questions.q: Which is NOT a benefit of tool consolidation?
options: Multiple specialized tools are required for full observability
More time for improving user experience
questions.explain: Consolidation means one platform replaces many specialized tools — the opposite of requiring several.

questions.q: What does OneAgent do once installed on a host?
options: Waits for you to configure each metric manually
Automatically captures logs, metrics, traces, and events and sends them to Dynatrace
Processes and stores all data locally
questions.explain: OneAgent collects automatically and ships data to Dynatrace; the platform does the heavy processing.

questions.q: In the star-map promotion example, what did root cause analysis reveal?
options: The promotion code had a bug
A traffic surge — the promo was working and capacity needed to be added
questions.explain: The slowdown came from a spike in visitors. The fix was more capacity, not pulling the promotion.

questions.q: Why doesn't a Dynatrace user need a powerful computer?
options: Dynatrace is SaaS — processing happens in Dynatrace's cloud
Data is sampled down to a few metrics
questions.explain: As SaaS, Dynatrace stores, processes, and analyzes data in the cloud. A browser is all you need.

questions.q: Grail answers large queries quickly mainly because it…
options: Keeps only one day of data
Uses massively parallel processing across many helper servers
Runs queries on the OneAgent hosts
questions.explain: Grail is a lakehouse with an MPP engine — many servers work on a query at once, scaling with demand.

questions.q: Which three things do Grail buckets control?
questions.explain: Buckets set how long data is kept, who can see it, and how it's organized.

questions.q: Why limit how long data is retained in a bucket?
options: To reduce licensing cost and keep sensitive data separated
Because Grail can't store more than 35 days
questions.explain: More retained data consumes more licensing, and separating data supports security.

questions.q: What is a custom-built Dynatrace App?
options: An app your team builds to run inside the Dynatrace platform for specific needs
An app that runs outside Dynatrace
questions.explain: Custom apps are built by your team and run within the platform. Prebuilt apps ship ready to use.

questions.q: Which OneAgent mode is the only one that captures service-level traces?
questions.explain: Full-Stack adds the service layer (traces and profiling) on top of host and process data.

questions.q: A chain of 500 point-of-sale terminals only needs "is it up?" visibility. Which mode fits best?
questions.explain: Foundation & Discovery has the lightest footprint — essential host data to confirm availability.

questions.q: Infrastructure mode collects which layers?
questions.explain: Infrastructure covers host and process metrics but no service tracing or profiling.

questions.q: Which list shows Smartscape's layers from top to bottom?
options: Hosts, Processes, Services, Applications, Data centers
Applications, Services, Processes, Hosts, Data centers
Applications, Processes, Services, Hosts, Data centers
Services, Applications, Hosts, Processes, Data centers
questions.explain: Applications → Services → Processes → Hosts → Data centers.

questions.q: How does Dynatrace represent databases in Smartscape?
options: As a special type of service
questions.explain: Databases aren't a separate layer; they're monitored as a special kind of service.

questions.q: To see the SQL queries an app sends, where must OneAgent be installed?
options: On the application server making the calls
questions.explain: Queries are captured on the calling side. Add Infrastructure mode on the DB host for its metrics.

questions.q: Three web servers serve the same site with identical processes. Dynatrace groups those processes into a…
questions.explain: A process group clusters processes doing the same job, usually across several hosts.

questions.q: A nightly job's service is missing when you view the last 15 minutes at noon. Most likely reason?
options: Services only appear when they received requests in the timeframe
questions.explain: No requests in the selected timeframe means no service data.

questions.q: In Dynatrace terms, which of these is an "application"?
options: A user-facing web or mobile front end
questions.explain: Dynatrace uses "application" narrowly: front ends real users interact with.

questions.q: A user clicks "Next" in a photo gallery and only the image area updates. What action type is this?
questions.explain: A background request that updates part of the page without a full reload is an XHR action.

questions.q: You add a web application detection rule for shop.example.com. What happens to last week's traffic?
options: It moves into the new application
questions.explain: Detection rules aren't retroactive — only new traffic is regrouped.

questions.q: With default thresholds, a page that loads in 5 seconds is rated…
questions.explain: 0–3 s satisfied, 3–15 s tolerating, over 15 s or any error frustrated.

questions.q: A page returns a 404 error in 0.3 seconds. Its Apdex rating is…
questions.explain: Errors count as frustrating no matter how fast the response.

questions.q: What must you do before setting a custom Apdex threshold on one specific user action?
options: Create a synthetic monitor for it
Mark it as a key user action
questions.explain: Per-action Apdex thresholds require the action to be a key user action.

questions.q: When should you use Agentless RUM?
options: When you can't install OneAgent on the web server
When you want more data than auto-injection
When the site has no JavaScript
questions.explain: Agentless RUM means pasting the JavaScript snippet yourself. It collects the same data as auto-injection.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT end a web user session?
questions.explain: Closing a tab doesn't end the session; closing the browser window does.

questions.q: You need to test a login → search → checkout journey every 15 minutes. Which synthetic monitor?
questions.explain: Clickpaths replay multi-step journeys (recorded with the Synthetic Recorder Chrome extension).

questions.q: How can a synthetic monitor test an app reachable only inside your network?
options: Install OneAgent on the app server
Use a private synthetic location on an ActiveGate, or allowlist Dynatrace IPs
questions.explain: Private synthetic locations run on an ActiveGate inside your network.

questions.q: Which statement about Session Replay is true?
options: It stores a video of the user's screen
It reconstructs the session from collected data, and passwords are always masked
It shows unmasked form data by default
questions.explain: Session Replay is a data-based reconstruction, not video. Sensitive content is masked by default; passwords always.

questions.q: Why does organizing a Dynatrace environment matter as it grows?
options: It makes filtering, searching, and managing large environments easier
It reduces the number of monitored hosts
It changes the data OneAgent collects
questions.explain: Organization is about findability and management — it powers filters, dashboards, and alerting.

questions.q: Identical prod and non-prod processes were merged into one process group. What fixes it?
options: Assign separate host groups, then restart the processes
Add a tag to each process
questions.explain: Host groups influence process group detection; the processes must restart to split.

questions.q: How many host groups can one host belong to?
questions.explain: A host belongs to exactly one host group.

questions.q: When is the best time to assign a host group?
questions.explain: Host groups are set at install; changing later means reinstalling or using oneagentctl.

questions.q: A service shows up as "svc-9876". Which tool makes it readable?
questions.explain: Naming rules change display names. They don't change what data is collected.

questions.q: Which is a typical use of tags?
options: Labeling entities for filtering, dashboards, alerting, and ownership
Limiting how long data is stored
questions.explain: Tags (often key:value, like Environment: Production) drive filtering, dashboards, alerting, and ownership.

questions.q: A new anomaly is detected that's related to an already-open problem. What does Dynatrace do?
options: Attaches the anomaly to the existing problem
questions.explain: Related anomalies are linked into the existing problem, avoiding duplicates.

questions.q: By default, how far above baseline must a metric be to count as an anomaly?
questions.explain: At least 50% above baseline, sustained. A 1 s baseline flags above 1.5 s.

questions.q: A service's baseline is 800 ms. Above what sustained value is an anomaly flagged?
How long until Dynatrace has a first baseline, and roughly how long until it's healthy?
questions.explain: First baseline after 2 hours, refined daily, healthy after about a week.

questions.q: Out of the box, static thresholds are mainly used for…
options: Infrastructure metrics like CPU and memory
questions.explain: Static thresholds cover infrastructure metrics. Baselines cover response time, failure rate, and traffic for apps and services.

questions.q: Which problem type is the most severe?
questions.explain: Availability > Error > Slowdown > Resource > Custom.

questions.q: A database CPU issue slows the app servers and web servers. Dynatrace reports…
options: One problem with the database as root cause
questions.explain: Using topology, Dynatrace groups related anomalies into one problem and avoids an alert storm.

questions.q: What does a maintenance window do?
options: Suppresses alerts (and optionally synthetics) during planned downtime
questions.explain: Maintenance windows prevent false alarms during planned work.

questions.q: You want a live, auto-refreshing view for the team during a sale. Use a…
questions.explain: Dashboards are for real-time views; notebooks capture point-in-time snapshots.

questions.q: What makes Notebooks different from Dashboards?
options: They save fixed snapshots of data at a point in time
questions.explain: Notebooks don't auto-refresh — ideal for preserving data from an event like Black Friday.

questions.q: What connects the steps in a DQL query?
questions.explain: Each step after | works on the output of the previous step, e.g. fetch logs | filter …

questions.q: Which statement about DQL is true?
options: It can't be used in dashboards
It queries data in Grail using commands like fetch and filter
It requires writing code from scratch every time
questions.explain: DQL talks to Grail. Dashboards and notebooks use it, and the apps can generate queries for you.

questions.q: Which apps are built specifically to explore raw log entries and distributed traces?
questions.explain: The Logs and Traces apps filter raw data from Grail and can generate DQL.

questions.q: Which of these can you do when editing a dashboard?
options: Change chart formats, tile titles, and filters
questions.explain: You can update titles, chart formats, filters, the default timeframe, and the dashboard's name.

questions.q: What is the Dynatrace Hub for?
questions.explain: The Hub is the "app store": prebuilt apps like Learn DQL and extensions like Tomcat or Kafka.

questions.q: Does Dynatrace activate every extension automatically when OneAgent is installed?
options: No — you enable what you need
questions.explain: Turning everything on would collect unneeded data and clutter the UI.

questions.q: A cloud integration with AWS, without OneAgent, gives you…
questions.explain: For logs, process metrics, services, and traces you still need OneAgent.

questions.q: A service runs on a technology Dynatrace doesn't instrument, and OneAgent can't be installed. How do you get its traces?
questions.explain: OpenTelemetry can send traces from outside OneAgent; they merge into unified traces.

questions.q: You need the cart total from requests on a host already running OneAgent. Which tool fits?
questions.explain: The OneAgent SDK adds request-level data on OneAgent-monitored processes. A business event rule could also extract it from logs or spans.

questions.q: Business events stored in the default bucket are kept for…
questions.explain: The default bizevents bucket retains them for 35 days.

questions.q: Which tool pushes Dynatrace data to Power BI or Excel?
questions.explain: Anything you can do in the UI you can do via the API, including exporting data.

questions.q: What handles monitoring for Kubernetes?
questions.explain: The Operator installs OneAgent in the cluster, collects metrics, and reports status.
